points.text: chlorocyclohexane as shown [cyclohexane ring with $\text{Cl}$ substituent]
cyclohexene would have absorption at 1500–1680 $(\text{cm}^{-1})$ because of $\text{C=C}$ (and adipic acid would not)
cyclohexene would have absorption at 3000–3100 $(\text{cm}^{-1})$ because of $\text{=C—H}$ / $\text{C—H}$ in alkene (and adipic acid would not)
adipic acid would have absorption at 2500–3000 $(\text{cm}^{-1})$ because of $\text{O—H}$ / $\text{CO}_{2}\text{—H}$ (and cyclohexene would not)
adipic acid would have absorption at 1040–1300 $(\text{cm}^{-1})$ because of $\text{C—O}$ (and cyclohexene would not)
adipic acid would have absorption at 1640–1750 $(\text{cm}^{-1})$ because of $\text{C=O}$ (and cyclohexene would not)
